Free Shipping Threshold Optimizer · guide

Where to set a free shipping threshold, and what it costs when you are wrong

Short answer: a free-shipping minimum earns money from three things and loses it on one. It earns from carts topped up to reach it, from buyers who no longer abandon at checkout, and from the fee you stop having to explain. It loses on the shipping you now pay for orders that would have reached the minimum anyway.

The arithmetic

  • Waived shipping costs the fee you would have collected on every order at or above the minimum.
  • A top-up earns your margin on the extra merchandise needed to reach the minimum, and costs the fee that cart would have paid.
  • Recovered buyers earn a whole order's contribution each; how many there are is the number nobody knows without testing.

Why the answer is a range, not a number

Past orders show you the first part exactly and say nothing about the last two. The optimizer therefore sweeps every round threshold, lets you set the top-up rate and the checkout drop-off, prints the drop-off at which each threshold breaks even, and picks a safe threshold: the one that is never far behind the best choice across a grid of both guesses.

Measure and test

  1. Export orders for the last month or two and keep subtotal and shipping cost.
  2. Paste them into the optimizer, or run node cli.mjs analyze orders.csv --current 75.
  3. Read the break-even drop-off beside each threshold and ask whether it is plausible for your store.
  4. Change the minimum for two or three weeks and compare average order value and conversion rate before keeping it.

Questions

Where should a free shipping threshold sit?

A common starting point is 15 to 30 percent above your average order value, so most shoppers are within reach of it but not already past it. The tool tests every round number against your own orders instead of relying on a rule of thumb.

Does free shipping over a minimum actually raise order value?

It can, when enough shoppers just under the minimum add an item to reach it. Whether that pays depends on your margin and on how much shipping you waive on orders that would have reached it anyway. The tool reports the checkout drop-off at which each minimum breaks even.

What if my shipping cost varies a lot by order?

Include a shipping cost per order. Heavy or distant orders that clear the threshold are the expensive ones to waive, and the tool uses each order's own cost when it has one.

FREE SHIPPING THRESHOLD OPTIMIZER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

What should your free shipping minimum be?

Paste your past orders — subtotal and what shipping cost you — and see what every minimum would earn, how many buyers each must win back to pay for the shipping you give away, and the threshold that loses least if your guesses are off.

Nothing is uploaded and no store is contacted. The text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device. Two behaviours — shoppers topping up their cart and buyers abandoning over shipping — cannot be read from past orders, so you set them and the result shows how much they matter.

Prefer a CLI, or want a CI check?

Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

node cli.mjs analyze orders.csv
cat orders.csv | node cli.mjs analyze -
node cli.mjs analyze orders.csv --current 75 --margin 45 --fee 5.95 --days 30
node cli.mjs analyze orders.csv --top-up 15 --drag 5 --json --fail-on warn

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: Where to set a free shipping threshold, and what it costs when you are wrong.

What's recognised

InputHandling

Top-up and checkout drop-off are assumptions you set (defaults: 25% of orders right under a threshold add items, fading to none 30% below it; 10% of buyers abandon when charged shipping); returns, repeat purchases and lifetime value are not modelled; margin is the profit share of merchandise before shipping.

Common questions

Does this connect to my store?

No. It reads the order rows you paste and never contacts Shopify, WooCommerce, Etsy or any carrier. Every figure is arithmetic on your numbers plus two behaviours you set, so nothing here is a measurement of your customers.

How do I get the numbers?

Export orders from your store and keep two columns: the merchandise subtotal before shipping and tax, and what you paid to ship it. In Shopify that is the Subtotal column of the orders export; the shipping cost comes from your carrier or label report. The shipping column is optional.

What is the top-up rate?

Of orders just under the free-shipping minimum, the share who add an item to reach it. It cannot be read off past orders, so you set it and the tool shows how the answer moves. 25% is a placeholder, not a benchmark.

What is checkout drop-off?

The share of would-be buyers who abandon when they have to pay shipping. Free shipping is mostly a bet that this number is large enough to pay for the shipping you give away, so the tool reports the drop-off at which each threshold breaks even rather than pretending to know yours.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The browser page runs on the text in your own browser and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.
